disposition_reason: Derived iron requirement and modeled risks of inadequate and excess intake for Indian women; no concentration measurements.

study.design: factorial requirement modeling with probability-approach risk estimation

period.as_reported: national household survey data (NSS 68th round, 2011 to 2012, as cited)

study.method: Monte Carlo convolution of basal and menstrual losses; EAR cut-point/probability method
study.qa: Validation against a biomarker survey in Uttar Pradesh

regulatory_or_exposure: EAR 14.4 mg/day (rounded 15 mg/day); RDA 30 or 35 mg/day (p. 368)
Tolerable upper level used 45 mg/day (p. 367; Table 2)
Risk of exceeding 45 mg/day with 10 mg/day fortification plus 14 mg/day supplementation: 0% to 54% by state (Rajasthan 54%) (Table 2)
Median state risk of inadequate intake 65% (IQR 48% to 78%) at the new EAR; 20% with fortification; 3% with fortification plus supplementation (Abstract; p. 369)
Weighted mean absorption from cereal-based Indian meals 8.7% (p. 368)
non_numeric_findings: Most dietary iron in India comes from cereals (about 70%) and about 1% from heme sources, per cited national survey data.
Fortification plus supplementation raises the risk of exceeding the upper level in some states.
